Junction Studio

Intersection and interchange option testing — Austroads AGRD Parts 3, 4A, 4B, 4C with TMR RPDM
v1.15.1 · MGA2020 Z56
Locate the site1
Junctions in the model2
Each junction has its own legs and its own arrangement (the option selected while it is being edited). Click one to edit it.
Link roads
A link road joins the end of one junction's leg to another's, with the first leg's cross-section and a ground-following profile. IPs are optional - without them the link curves between the two leg tangents.
Approaches3
Drag the numbered pins on the map to set each leg's bearing. Grade blank = taken from the ground model.
Arc through the junction
Sign is the direction you turn driving from the first named leg towards the junction and on through. Side roads stay straight and radial to the arc. Service interchanges bend as a whole on the arc (crossroad radial, ramp radii kept); on every interchange the freeway shoulders and median barrier are set for sight distance and curve widening.
Design basis4
Batters, traffic and unit rates
Verges per AGRD Part 3 Table 4.9. Behind a likely barrier the verge widens so the barrier face is the working width from the batter hinge (min 1.0 m) - use the chosen product's tested working width.
Unit rates for the cost index (ranking only, not an estimate):
Forms to test5
Background Overlays
Drag to orbit · right-drag to pan · wheel to zoom
Scoring weights
Each criterion is scaled across the generated options (best = 1, worst = 0) and weighted. Capacity only counts once turning counts are entered on the Traffic tab.
Peak-hour turning movements (veh/h)
Rows are where traffic comes from, columns where it goes. The letter under each cell is the turn (L left, T through, R right, U U-turn). Example counts are scaled from road class and are not real data.
From \ To
Indicative only: priority uses gap acceptance, signals use critical flow ratios with 5 s lost per phase, roundabouts use HCM 6 entry capacity, freeways 2000 pcu/h/lane and single-lane ramps 1800 veh/h. Use SIDRA or a network model for design.
Plot to PDF
A drawing sheet per option: hatched plan to scale over the imagery, title block with the road names and intersection type, scale bar, north point, legend and notes. Set the road names in step 1.
12d Model (.12da)
Strings in MGA2020 Zone 56 with levels, UTF-16LE with BOM and CRLF. Control lines carry per-vertex radius_data (positive right-hand). Line marking uses the TMR V15.1.1 MRR_L* linestyles (MRR_LLL1, MRR_LEL2, MRR_LGW...) with the AS 1742.2 code as an attribute. Sight lines, swept paths, markings and control lines are flagged non-tinable. One model per option.
IFC 4.3 (.ifc)
IfcAlignment with horizontal and vertical semantic segments, IfcPavement and IfcKerb tessellated surfaces, line marking as IfcSurfaceFeature (LINEMARKING / SYMBOLMARKING / HATCHMARKING) adhering to the pavement, strings as IfcAnnotation, IfcMapConversion to EPSG:7856. Opens in BimAnalyser.
CAD plan (.dxf)
2D plan drawing in MGA2020 Zone 56 (AutoCAD R12 DXF - opens in AutoCAD, Civil 3D, BricsCAD, MicroStation, 12d and QGIS; Save As in AutoCAD for a DWG). Layers JS-* by string type, surface and AS 1742.2 marking code (prefixed with the option id for all options), line marking at its painted width with a linetype per dash pattern, structures, alignment names and 50 m chainage ticks.
Google Earth (.kml)
Option strings as WGS84 lines for stakeholder review.
Tables
Option comparison and the compliance ledger as CSV, the project as JSON to reopen later.
